[2026-09-02 | AMZN | Underweight | -1.2% | -0.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: trim existing exposure by roughly one-third to one-half, taking a standard allocation to ~50–60%, and execute at least three-quarters of that reduction at market near $254.98 rather than posting sell limits above spot — the last two windows showed AMZN does not owe us a bounce, and the bull's own add-triggers ($260.4–$263.66 on >40M shares) sit above the current price. Do not initiate or add at $254.98, and do not short a name with $176.1B of liquid assets and a rising 50/200-day structure. Carry the residual with a hard stop on a daily close below $250.64 (breach opens $238.87, the 200-day inside the unfilled July gap, −6.3%), sized so that gap is a bad quarter, not a portfolio event. Rebuild only on a reclaim of $260.4–$263.66 on >40M shares with the MACD histogram turning positive and RSI back above 55 — half the trimmed amount at confirmation, the rest on a higher low above $260 — and only with at least one fundamental gate cleared. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three seats converged on reducing AMZN; they split only on size and re-entry mechanics, so the work here is deciding which critique of execution is strongest — and on that the conservative and neutral seats beat the aggressive seat's confidence, while the aggressive seat beats the conservative seat's rigidity.

**What decides the direction.** The bull's operating case is not contested and I credit it fully: Q2 2026 revenue $200.6B (+19.6%), operating income $27.5B (+43.2%), margin 13.7% (+226 bps), H1 operating income $51.3B (+36.6%), higher lows intact at $198.79 → $225.55 → $226.16 → $251.93, price $254.98 above a rising 50-day ($252.83) and 6.7% above a rising 200-day ($238.87). That is why this is not a Sell. What decides the rating is that the price no longer pays for the risk being carried. Three items did it. First, cash conversion and leverage: TTM FCF is −$11.6B versus +$13.5B a year ago, Q2 FCF −$8.8B on $54.2B of quarterly capex (27.0% of revenue, 2.3x D&A), long-term debt $68.8B → $133.0B in six months (+93%), net cash down 42.4% to $29.7B, Q2 interest expense +155% to $1.3B. The aggressive seat is right that "deliberate investment" explains the capex but does not neutralize the point that D&A (+31.3% YoY) and interest are now rising fast enough to pressure the very margin expansion being underwritten — and the 0.91x gross-debt/OCF ratio is flattered by deferred taxes ($4.0B of H1 cash taxes against a $27.8B provision). Second, earnings quality: $62.8B of non-cash private-equity revaluation gains equal roughly 78% of H1 pre-tax income, so core EPS is ~$4.11 against reported $8.53 (Q2 ~$2.16 vs $5.75); annualized, AMZN trades near 30–31x core earnings with negative FCF, and the mark carries headline risk if private AI/tech valuations reset. Third, the tape: close below the 10 EMA ($259.36), VWMA ($260.38) and 20-day basis ($263.66), a widening negative MACD histogram at −1.585, RSI 46.38 with an August bearish divergence, only a 0.85% cushion above the 50-day, and a failed +4.0% bounce on 49.5M shares followed by 24.0M (thinnest in three weeks) — absorption, not accumulation.

**Where each seat wins on execution.** The aggressive seat wins the core mechanical point, and it is the one the trader got right: the $250.64 stop is $4.34 from spot against a $6.93 ATR (2.72%), so it bounds intent, not loss. Protection must come from reducing exposure now, not from a stop after the fact — and "if there is no edge initiating at $254.98, there is no edge holding full size" is directionally correct for a caller with no cost-basis or mandate constraint. But the aggressive seat is too confident that trim-and-rebuild is close to free: a reclaim of $260.4–$263.66 means buying back higher after a loss, and a $250–260 chop produces exactly the whipsaw he waves away. The conservative seat wins the sizing argument and the gap-risk realism (a −5.6% day and a +15.3% day have both printed this year; the move to $238.87 arrives as a gap, not a trend), but his demand for a hard fundamental catalyst — positive FCF or debt stabilization — before rebuilding is too strict for a capital-intensive buildout that may hold FCF negative for several quarters by design, and would convert a trim inside an intact primary uptrend into a permanent underweight. The neutral seat is closest to right: staged, evidence-linked rebuild rather than a freeze-out. I therefore take the trader's 50–60% band, push a caller who is concentrated or cannot tolerate the $238.87 gap to the conservative's lower end (~50%), and adopt the neutral's two-step rebuild **plus** the conservative's requirement of at least one fundamental check, because a purely technical re-entry into a mark-to-model, negative-FCF print is buying the narrative back.

**Why Underweight and not Sell, and not Hold.** Underweight, not Sell, because there is no solvency or permanent-capital-loss case: $176.1B of liquid assets, still net cash at +$29.7B, ~24x interest coverage, $650B of contractual obligations with $78.1B due within twelve months, and a rising 50/200-day with the golden cross intact. The record in this name is unambiguous that heavy de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure (07-22 through 07-30) cost 12–22% of five-day alpha, which is exactly why a real residual core is kept. Underweight, not Hold, because full weight at $254.98 is the worst-priced option on the board: ~2–3% to the first bull trigger that itself requires volume confirmation, against −6.3% to the 200-day, with negative FCF, debt-funded capex, inflated headline EPS and a deteriorating intermediate trend all pointing the same way. Holding here is not neutral; it is an unhedged bet that the capex-to-cash bridge closes before the depreciation bill lands.

**What would change the call.** Upgrades require evidence, not narrative: (a) a daily close above $260.4–$263.66 on >40M shares with the MACD histogram positive and RSI >55, rebuilt in two steps; and/or (b) TTM FCF turning positive or capex/revenue stabilizing below ~25%; (c) net cash no longer falling and interest-expense growth decelerating; (d) disclosure confirming whether the private-equity revaluation gains recur. Downgrades: a daily close below $250.64 halves the residual; a decisive break of the 50-day at $252.83/ the $250.64 shelf with expanding volume opens $238.87 and argues for taking the residual toward minimum; any markdown on the revaluation book is a Sell trigger, and because it arrives as a gap, exposure must already be small when it happens. No averaging down anywhere on that ladder.

**Data gaps I am not underwriting.** The supplied news window covered only 20 of 172 records with no hard AMZN catalyst in either direction — that is a data gap, not a signal, and I read it neither bullishly nor bearishly. There is no verification of capex returns, no forward guidance detail, no segment-level AWS revenue or margin in the record, no identity or valuation inputs for the revaluation book, and no portfolio, holdings, cost basis or cash context, so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should flex with the caller's aggregate AI-capex exposure elsewhere. Finally, per the 08-26 lesson: the fundamental leg here is untested and will only be scored at the Q3 print — the five-day tape is noise and must not be read as confirmation of the cash-flow thesis.

**Price Target**: 246.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The five days delivered −1.2% raw and −0.3% alpha versus SPY — directionally consistent with Underweight, but a 0.3% spread is noise, and five days against a 3–6 month horizon cannot judge the call either way. The window mildly supports the tape leg (no bounce materialized after the failed 49.5M-share rally, so the absorption read held) while saying nothing about the cash-conversion and earnings-quality core, which was explicitly deferred to the Q3 print; if anything, a −0.3% alpha undercuts any claim that the trim was an alpha-generating de-risk rather than mostly beta. Lesson for next time: write the scoring rule into the call itself — pre-commit to judging this thesis at the Q3 print over a ≥1-month window — so a ±0.3% five-day alpha is never retroactively read as confirmation of a fundamental argument it never tested.

[2026-09-01 | AMZN | Underweight | -1.0% | -1.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: trim 30–40% of a standard position to ~0.5–0.6x standard, in three staged pieces rather than one bet on the tape. Take a first 10–15% slice at market now in the $254.92–256.26 area, leave resting limits for another 10–15% in the $258.58–262.01 shelf, and complete the reduction only on a daily close below $251.50 — the true confluence break beneath the 50-SMA $252.41, lower Bollinger $251.61 and 09-01 low $251.93, not a half-ATR wiggle at $252.41. Do not exit and do not short: a rising 200-SMA ($238.79) plus 43.2% operating-income growth make short stock poor risk/reward; if the desk wants downside convexity, use a small defined-risk put spread sized as insurance, and do not sell calls into $266.43–$267.56 without verified implied volatility (we have none). On a close below $251.50, halve the residual again toward ~0.25x; re-add only on a close above $256.26 with the 10-EMA no longer falling and two narrowing MACD-histogram sessions, a volume-backed reclaim of $261.08/$262.01 on 40–45M shares, or a flush into $239.82–$245.34 holding on declining volume. Horizon 1–3 months, re-scored on the Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not contested by anyone in the room — Research Manager, trader and all three risk seats land on reduce — so the decision is about size and instrumentation, and on both the aggressive and conservative seats each won one exchange and overreached on the other.

The bear won the two arguments that price the equity for the next one to two quarters. First, the valuation denominator: TTM capex (~$173B) now exceeds TTM EBITDA (~$170B), so the 16.6x EV/EBITDA headline is a pre-capex number for a business reinvesting 100%+ of it. On EBITDA-less-maintenance-capex that is ~29x and on annualized core EPS ~33x, against TTM free cash flow of −$11.6B, H1 −$27.0B, Q2 −$8.8B — negative on every horizon — with no buyback and no dividend to put a bid under the stock. The specific derivations are analyst arithmetic rather than vendor prints and I treat them as directional, but the direction is unrefuted and the bull never answered it on the merits. Second, earnings quality: ~$50.5B of the $80.9B Q2 pretax income was a non-cash markup of a private holding that went $16.2B → $122.3B in six months — ~11% of assets — so core Q2 EPS is ~$1.95 against a reported $5.75. Anyone capitalizing trailing reported EPS of ~$12 is overstating recurring earnings roughly twofold. Layered on that, long-term debt went $68.8B → $133.0B (+96%), interest expense +155%, the current ratio is 1.03x, and $650B of contractual obligations carries $78.1B due inside twelve months against $161.4B TTM operating cash flow. The neutral is right that a 1.03x current ratio and a $650B lease/purchase ladder are normal for AMZN's negative-working-capital model and a liquidity-management issue rather than a solvency one — but they are not a cushion either, and the $650B is a schedule of what AMZN owes, not the "demand visibility" the bull claimed. Third, the D&A lag: TTM depreciation of $75.2B growing 32% against a ~$217B annualized capex run-rate means a multi-year wave of incremental depreciation is already committed; the specific $25B/quarter figure is aggressive because buildings depreciate over decades and servers over five to six years, but the structural point holds — part of the 230bp of margin expansion is the accounting gap between cash out and cost recognition, and that gap closes. The bull answered with assertion, not arithmetic.

The tape decided entry quality, and it decided it against adding. At $254.92 AMZN sits below a falling 10-EMA ($260.33) and the VWMA ($261.08), the 08-17 bearish MACD cross has re-widened (histogram −1.454), RSI 46.33 is not washed out, and the 08-28 push to $267.56 died in two sessions. R:R to the first real target ($264.55) is ~1.14:1 with five resistance layers before $272; the bull's 2.7:1 requires skipping T1 and a stop ($246.50) that sits inside a $7.245 ATR. And the 50-SMA at $252.41 is rising on arithmetic, not strength — the $274–$284 early-August closes roll out of the window in mid-to-late September — while the golden-cross spread has compressed from $22.16 on 07-06 to $13.62 and the 10-EMA is falling toward the 50-SMA. That is why I side with the conservative on the execution question the neutral framed: the aggressive's "work the whole trim into $258.58–$262.01" is internally inconsistent with his own broken-tape case, and the aggressive is right to be criticized for a fallback that sells into the knife. The conservative's insight — that risk management cannot depend on the market cooperating with our preferred price — is the one that governs, and it is also the documented lesson from this book: the 8/25 GOOGL and the 8/20 AMZN reviews both showed a first tranche gated behind a 1% rally into resistance converting a correct call into relative drag. So the first slice goes at market now, the shelf carries a resting limit for the balance, and the true confluence break at $251.50 — not the 252.41 level the neutral correctly identified as a half-ATR wiggle — completes the trim.

Where the aggressive and the conservative both overreach: the aggressive wants to sell calls into $266.43–$267.56, but ATR has contracted 27% from the 08-05 peak to $7.245, there is no implied-volatility data in this round, and capping recovery at exactly the ceiling where the last two rallies died on an operating business growing operating income 43.2% is selling cheap optionality to hedge a risk better handled by smaller size. The conservative's demand for an additional cut on a close below $252.41 is inside half an ATR and will whipsaw; his five-session time stop converts a price-and-confirmation process into a calendar, and if AMZN chops between $253 and $257 it forces a print into exactly the confluence he warned about. I also adopt the neutral's correction on the gap: the unfilled $239.82–$262.01 zone is a scenario, not a magnet — the 200-SMA has already risen from $233.03 on 07-06 to $238.79 on 09-01, so by the time price arrives the structural support will likely be nearer $240–$242. It is a legitimate downside reference, not a base case.

Why Underweight and not Sell, and why the residual is not token. Nothing in the bear case is a solvency case or a permanent-capital-loss case, and the franchise line items are genuinely strong: revenue +19.6% to $200.6B (first $200B quarter), operating income +43.2% to $27.5B, margin 13.7% (+230bp), marketing +2.5%, G&A −6%, SBC −7.6%, $176.1B of cash and AFS securities, ~0.4x net leverage excluding leases, ~21x interest coverage, price +6.76% above a rising 200-SMA with the golden cross intact since May. The bear explicitly declined to short, and his own prescription — trim into strength, wait for the $261–262 reclaim or a flush to $240–245 — is a de-risking instruction, not a bearish thesis; I read it that way. The record in this name reinforces it: prior AMZN Underweights that de-risked hard inside an intact rising 50/200-SMA structure cost 12–22% of five-day alpha, and the 8/21 trim earned +2.5%. Sell would also abandon a residual that is the only instrument for participating in a capex inflection we cannot yet rule out. Full weight, however, is the worst-priced option on the board: a quarter of the upside to the first ceiling against a dollar of downside to the 50-SMA, with two genuinely unpriced tails — a mark reset on the $122.3B private holding (which the bull put on his own "change my mind" list) and an FTC advertising-auction remedy aimed precisely at the highest-margin profit pool where incremental margin comes from. Unquantifiable is not immaterial, and the bull treated it as zero.

What would change the call. Upward to Overweight requires all of: (a) Q3 operating margin at or above 13.7%; (b) quarterly capex at or below the $54.2B Q2 print — a step-up keeps free cash flow broken and is the bear case in its purest form; (c) evidence of AWS share retention, with the $35B Anthropic–Lambda award going to a neocloud as a warning rather than a non-event; (d) clarity on the shape of any FTC advertising remedy, since a behavioral constraint on auction mechanics hits the profit pool for years; (e) disclosure or mark movement on the $122.3B private holding plus AOCI/AFS rate sensitivity (+$38.1B H1 OCI against only −$1.6B disclosed FX). Technically, restoration toward 0.65–0.75x requires a close above $256.26 with the 10-EMA no longer falling and two narrowing histogram sessions, or a volume-backed reclaim of $261.08/$262.01 on 40–45M shares. Downward to Sell requires a close below $251.50 that fails to reclaim $253 within two to three sessions, a break of the rising 200-SMA, an impairment or flat mark on the private book, or net cash crossing to net debt while capex stays above $50B/quarter.

Data explicitly not underwritten: insider activity is DATA UNAVAILABLE in this round — unknown, not neutral — so it is weighted zero in both directions; no implied-volatility data exists, so any option overlay is unpriceable and must be treated as optional rather than recommended; AWS segment revenue and operating margin were not returned, so the AWS-acceleration justification for capex is inference, not evidence; the FTC matter has no complaint details, damages or requested remedy; cash EBITDA, annualized core EPS and incremental D&A are analyst derivations from the two notes rather than vendor prints; and with no portfolio, holdings or cash context, all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should flex with the caller's aggregate AI-capex exposure elsewhere — trimming AMZN while holding MSFT, GOOGL, NVDA and neoclouds at full weight would be optics, not risk management.

**Price Target**: 250.0
